## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components, combined with a fused scatter for respawn+render, can approach the streaming ceiling across death rates.

## Layout & approach
The AoS layout at 69 B/particle offers 28 hot bytes (41%) to loop 1 (age+pos+vel) and 32 (47%) to loop 2 (color+pos+seed), with 1 B/particle mask intermediate; the remaining 53–59% is dead weight on every 68 B stride. Loop 1 is Halide-expressible and vectorization-friendly; loop 2 fuses respawn and render, scattering byte-granular RGB writes into a framebuffer. The working set spills L1d at N≈949 and L2 at N≈60787, but the ~41–47% hot fraction makes the effective working set roughly half the nominal 69·N.

## Cache saturation
The ns/particle curve is flat across all regimes: at q=0.01 it holds 7.3–8.0 ns/p from N=380 (L1d) through N=10M (DRAM), with no knee at either spill — cost even dips in DRAM (7.25 at N=150000 vs 7.38 at N=380). The 41–47% hot fraction and 68 B stride are prefetch-friendly enough that DRAM latency hides behind compute. At higher q the curve shifts upward uniformly (q=0.5: ~12.7–12.9 ns/p across all N), confirming added cost is per-particle compute, not cache hierarchy.

## Bandwidth
The memory floor is 2.308 ns/p; at q=0.01 the algo runs 7.3–8.0 ns/p (3.2–3.5× the floor), achieving 9.3–9.5 GB/s — 31% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling. This is compute/overhead-bound. Bandwidth falls with death rate (9.3→5.4 GB/s, q=0.01→0.5) as branch overhead crowds out useful work. Against baseline it is essentially even: 1.01× at q=0.01, 0.92× at q=0.25. Against the winner it is 1.7–2.0× slower at q=0.01, worsening to 2.2–2.4× at q=0.5 — the branchy fused scatter erases any vectorization gain.

## Assembly
Loop 1 achieves partial vectorization: `dup.4s`, `fmul.4s`, `fadd.4s`, `ext.16b` on position/velocity four-wide with `ld1.s` for indexed velocity — but only 6 of 10 FP ops are vectorized. Loop 2 is the bottleneck: 284 insns/iter, 30 conditional branches, 19 `csel`, 21 byte-granular `strb` stores. Each framebuffer pixel needs three `ldrb`/`add`/`cmp`/`csel`/`strb` sequences (0x10004db28–0x10004db6c, replicated thrice), and respawn calls `bl _layouts.ML01.data.Data.spawn` per dead particle. The 18 vector instructions concentrate in loop 1; loop 2's 31 scalar FP ops cannot stream. Branch_flush rises from 2.5% (q=0.01) to 20.2% (q=0.5).

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo matches naive everywhere (0.92–1.01× baseline) and never approaches the winner (1.7–2.4× slower). At q=0.01 it sustains only 31% of ceiling despite loop 1's partial `fmul.4s` vectorization, because loop 2's 284-instruction fused scatter with 21 `strb` stores and 30 branches cannot stream. At q=0.5 branch_flush reaches 20.2% and the algo is 2.4× slower than the winner. The fused scatter's byte-granular writes and per-particle respawn call dominate regardless of death rate or cache regime.
